source.title: More is Less: The Pitfalls of Multi-Model Synthetic Preference Data in DPO Safety Alignment
source.authors: Yi-Fan Wang; Run-Jin Chen; Bo-Lian Li; David Cho; Yihe Deng; Ruqi Zhang; Tian-Long Chen; Zhang-Yang Wang; A. Grama; Junyuan Hong

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports safety outcomes from DPO preference-data pipelines, but does not test the listed claims about harmful or benign supervised fine-tuning, token-position KL, opening-token bypasses, localized weights, or deepening safety beyond initial tokens. The cited original sources are not tested.
record.gate_note: The paper reports jailbreak ASR after DPO training with different preference-data sources, plus some data controls and online-DPO results. These results concern safety behavior but do not test any listed version. General-task scores, toxicity scores, training-loss plots, and linear-classifier separability results are not rows because they do not measure a listed version's specified behavior.
record.test_reason: The study compares preference-data sources for DPO safety training of SFT'd base models and reports jailbreak ASR. It does not fine-tune safety-trained models on harmful or benign data (V1, V2). It does not measure per-token KL (V3), prefill, suffix or decoding attacks (V4), or parameter localization (V5). Its 'superficial cues' explanation concerns chosen/rejected separability in preference data, not safety depth across token positions (V6). It does not test token-depth deepening (V7). It cites the original sources only, for scoring rules and spurious refusal keywords.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors also conclude that general-task performance is similar across data sources, so the effect is specific to safety. They attribute the failure to high linear separability of multi-model chosen/rejected pairs, which enables reward hacking on superficial cues; DPO loss collapses quickly for GPT4o+Self. They report that a beta and learning-rate ablation does not fix it.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies DPO preference-data construction and safety outcomes, rather than the supervised fine-tuning, token-distribution, or token-depth methods in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported safety ASR varies with preference-data source and model. The paper also reports different ASR after length control, format cleaning, and relevance filtering; these controls do not substantially solve the authors' identified vulnerability.

fits_no_version.finding: Across six 7B-8B models, Self+RM DPO data gives the lowest GPT-ASR. Direct pairing with human, GPT-4o or stronger-model chosen responses gives the highest, e.g. Llama-3.1-8B 0.64 vs 0.16. The same ordering holds at 13B/14B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In safety DPO, preference data whose chosen and rejected responses come from different sources yields higher jailbreak ASR than self-generated, reward-model-ranked pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: Online DPO with Self+RM data on Llama-3.1-8B lowers GPT-ASR from 0.56 (SFT) to 0.05 after three iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Iterative self-generated, reward-model-ranked DPO progressively reduces jailbreak ASR.

fits_no_version.finding: Length, format and relevance controls on HC+Self data leave ASR near 0.51 (0.49, 0.60, 0.53).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Simple surface-feature controls do not fix the safety failure of multi-source preference data.

record.problems: The main safety evaluation uses the first 100 AdvBench examples and GPT-4o as judge; ASR is defined by responses receiving a score of 5. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The model used for the Table 2 controlled comparisons is not stated in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded Keyword ASR and GPT-Score from Table 4 because GPT-ASR is the paper's primary safety metric; excluded IPO, HH-RLHF, toxicity, and parameter-ablation results because they do not measure a listed claim version's specified behavior. Also excluded training-loss and linear-separability analyses because they do not report the harmful-compliance behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: Whether harmful fine-tuning of a safety-trained model raises harmful compliance; no harmful fine-tuning of an aligned model is done.
Whether benign fine-tuning erodes existing safety; the DPO training here is safety-targeted and starts from SFT'd base models.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes; only plain AdvBench prompts are used.
Localization of safety in a few weights or ranks.
Whether data or objective causes safety to concentrate in early tokens. The reward-hacking and separability analysis is about preference-pair cues, not token depth.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and how robust it is.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation and tranche (cites_only, T6) are confirmed. The 'superficial patterns' framing is a different construct from token-depth shallowness, so it is not a V6 test. Excluded results are declared in rows_left_out: KW-ASR, GPT-Score, IPO, HH-RLHF, toxicity and the beta ablation (ASR 0.53-0.57). None of them bears on a version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a few to a few hundred harmful examples in fine-tuning cause a safety-trained model to comply.
Whether ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Whether compliant prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes bypass refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether the data or objective causes safety to be shallow specifically in response-token depth.
Whether training that spreads safety beyond initial tokens deepens safety and remains robust.
